name: P10
rule_text: P10 probe rule (shared iteration-10 text; unspecified details fixed by NOV-R and committed). TRACE POOL, built in this order: reference in [BF, FF, WF, AWF, c12 (bp.prio_c12_vec, the vectorised FunSearch OR heuristic), c14 (bp.prio_c14, the FunSearch Weibull heuristic)]; then instance in P1SRC-W (5 x 5,000 items, capacity 100) followed by P1SRC-OR (5 x 500 items, capacity 150); then item order. Each instance contributes bp.pack_trace(items, cap, ref) states (item, opened bins that fit in index order, n_empty, chosen capacity); pool size 6 x 27,500 = 165,000. rng = numpy.random.default_rng(20261024); idx = np.sort(rng.choice(165000, size=1000, replace=False)); the 1,000 trace states are the pool rows at idx, stored as [item, opened_fit, n_empty, instance capacity]. UNIFORM STATES, continuing the same rng, for i in 0..999: cap = 100 if i is even else 150; item = rng.integers(1, cap+1); n_open = 0 if item == cap else rng.integers(1, 31); opened = rng.integers(item, cap, size=n_open) (remaining capacities in [item, cap-1] in generated order; no draw when n_open == 0); n_empty = rng.integers(1, 31). States: trace states first, then uniform states. A state is informative when the reconstructed valid array opened_fit + [cap]*n_empty holds at least 2 distinct capacities (exactly as sandbox._load_probe builds it). Decisions: the remaining capacity of the chosen bin, int(arr[argmax(priority(item, arr.copy()))]); 65535 on error.
